messages:
maya: :rotating_light: noticing spike in 5xx from hosted inference after the 03:40 canary deploy. Dash shows 503s and downstream timeouts. Can we triage?
darren: saw it too, starts ~03:42 UTC. Customer-reported latency up. Traces point to auth-proxy calls timing out.
sre-oncall: on it. Pulling logs and traces now. Any config flags flipped in the canary? @deploy-bot, what changed in today's rollout?
deploy-bot: canary 2026-03-18T03:35 UTC: feature_flags: {"auth_prefetch": true, "binary_prefetch_v2": true} deployed to 8% seed traffic.
maya: thanks. suspecting "auth_prefetch" — telemetry shows auth latency tail increased ~150ms -> 800ms.
darren: logs: repeated upstream errors from auth-proxy: 
```
[03:42:11] upstream_read_timeout from auth-proxy host=auth-svc-2
[03:42:12] 503 Service Unavailable gateway=ingress-gw
[03:42:15] kvcache miss fallback -> extra auth calls
```
sre-oncall: good find. Looks like the flag enables a sync lookup on every request for warmup, causing thundering on auth-svc under canary.
jamie: paging auth-service owners to confirm connection pool behavior under this pattern. @darren can you confirm connection counts?
darren: connection_count to auth-svc jumped from ~200 -> ~1200 on canary workers. CPU on auth-svc spiked and started rejecting.
sre-oncall: that explains 5xx cascade. Plan: 1) roll back flag in canary 2) scale auth-svc more if rollback doesn't clear 3) confirm prefix/KV cache TTL.
maya: agree. Who can flip the flag rollback? @jamie?
jamie: I can rollback the canary flag to previous state for seed traffic now. Initiating rollback and will monitor.
supportops-bot: customer-facing incident ticket created: INC-3319. Notifying affected customers with status update template.
deploy-bot: rollback action queued: revert feature_flags.auth_prefetch -> false on canary (8%) at 03:46 UTC.
jamie: rolled back at 03:46:45 UTC. Monitoring.
darren: post-rollback: auth latency tail back to ~160ms within 2m. 5xx rate trending down.
sre-oncall: observing gateway 503s drop to baseline. Marking immediate P1 mitigated but keep incident open for root cause and follow-up.
maya: we should add guardrail to prevent sync auth calls under canary — maybe make it async or add circuit-breaker. Also add a preflight load test for flags that touch auth.
jamie: filing a GH issue with steps to repro locally and a proposal for feature flag scoping to avoid global sync.
darren: repro steps I used: 
```
# short repro script hitting canary variant header
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "X-Seed-Weight: 8" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .status & done
```
sre-oncall: collect traces: span ids 0x7a3f..0x7a9b show auth-svc wait spikes. Saving to incident channel.
supportops-bot: updated customers: "We identified a canary config that caused increased auth latency; we've rolled it back. We'll follow up with postmortem and mitigation timeline."
maya: next steps: (a) postmortem, (b) add rollout checklist item: "no synchronous auth-prefetch enabled during early seed", (c) add metric alert for auth connection count jump.
jamie: assigning follow-ups: #1 GH-4582 rollback review (jamie), #2 perf test for flag (darren), #3 billing/customer check-in (maya).
sre-oncall: closing P1 once on-call confirms 30m stable window. Will re-open if regressions recur.
maya: thanks team. Good catch and quick rollback :thumbsup:
